description:
OPIC Open Intelligent Computing Platform OPIC is an ontology-driven intelligent computing + MaaS platform: 23 capability domains form a complete semantic layer, covering the full path from physical compute onboarding to AI application consumption.
Three differentiators Ontology-driven requirements engineering — requirements are a machine-verifiable semantic system: one Requirements Specification plus one Editorial Note per domain, gated by 927 automated checks, a consistency scan (130 cross-domain references, zero dangling links), and 13 self-checks in Chapter 9; the baseline is frozen by a SHA-256 manifest. Layer 3 is fully swappable — all open-source dependencies are isolated in the dependency layer; swapping an engine does not trigger requirement changes except when the swap exposes a semantic gap. All 20 industry-benchmark must-haves met (2026-09 refresh: batch inference, structured output, guardrail as independent API, split caching billing, model retirement commitments, etc.). Snapshot (requirements baseline v3.2) Metric Value Capability domains 23 Spec / editorial lines 47,628 / 9,421 Machine checks 927 · FAIL 0 / WARN 0 Cross-domain refs 130 · broken 0 Four review rounds 88 findings · 86 closed / 2 tracked

Ontology Engineering Method (core differentiator) The fundamental difference from “requirements doc + development”: requirements are a computable, verifiable, freezable semantic system.
Nine cross-cutting criteria ① explicit source of truth ② write-path convergence ③ credential lineage across eight positions ④ append-only ledger ⑤ approval-decision families (irreversible-failure / boundary-expansion; no approval without an alternative mechanism) ⑥ five execution paradigms ⑦ no-side-effect execution family ⑧ recompute-cost criterion ⑨ enforcement at the consumer side.
